Sarunyu has a stick of length 1 with one endpoint marked in red. Every minute, he picks one of his sticks uniformly at random and breaks it into two halves of equal length. Compute the expected length of the stick with the red endpoint after 5 minutes.

message.content:
Let \(L_t\) be the length of the red-endpoint stick after \(t\) minutes.

After \(t\) minutes, there are \(t+1\) sticks. If the red stick is chosen at the next minute, its length is halved; otherwise it stays the same. Since it is chosen with probability \(1/(t+1)\),

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_{t+1}\mid L_t]
= L_t\left(\frac{1}{t+1}\cdot \frac12+\frac{t}{t+1}\cdot 1\right)
= L_t\left(1-\frac{1}{2(t+1)}\right).
\]

Thus

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_5]
= \prod_{t=0}^{4}\left(1-\frac{1}{2(t+1)}\right)
= \left(\frac12\right)\left(\frac34\right)\left(\frac56\right)\left(\frac78\right)\left(\frac9{10}\right).
\]

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_5]
= \frac{1\cdot 3\cdot 5\cdot 7\cdot 9}{2\cdot 4\cdot 6\cdot 8\cdot 10}
= \frac{945}{3840}
= \frac{63}{256}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{63}{256}}
\]
